2610.19927.title: Deterministic and Programmable Fusion for Scalable Generation of Photonic Graph States
2610.19927.abstract: Entanglement in multiphoton graph states is an important resource with various applications, such as measurement-based quantum computing and memory-less quantum repeaters. While some primitive instances have been successfully prepared, scalable generation of large-scale graph states with programmable connections remains an outstanding challenge. Fusion provides a promising "divide-and-conquer" approach by linking smaller resource states into larger, more complex graphs. However, its practical scalability has been limited by the probabilistic nature of conventional fusion protocols, which necessitates extensive hardware overhead and feed-forward resources to achieve deterministic outcomes. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a deterministic fusion operation with built-in error mitigation, capable of connecting small time-bin-encoded cluster states--originally generated on-demand from a quantum emitter--into larger, reconfigurable photonic graph states of increased sizes. The fusion operation is realized by nondestructively projecting pairs of flying microwave photonic qubits into Bell states using superconducting circuits with in-situ programmability. Crucially, the protocol features active reset and reuse of matter qubits during graph state generation, thereby circumventing the coherence constraints of the quantum emitter and enabling the generation of genuine multipartite entanglement across 13 photonic qubits. Our results establish a scalable framework for photonic graph-state synthesis, paving the way for fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation and distributed quantum networks.
2610.19927.why: Bell-state projection of flying microwave photons fuses on-demand time-bin cluster states deterministically, reaching genuine 13-photon entanglement with emitter reset and reuse.

eli5.plain: They stitched small batches of entangled microwave photons into one bigger entangled web, and the stitching works every time rather than by luck.
eli5.how: A superconducting emitter makes short chains of entangled photons in time bins; a second circuit catches pairs of photons and checks, without destroying them, which Bell state they share, which glues the chains together. The emitter qubit is reset and reused between chains.
eli5.matters: Fusing is the step that turns a single emitter into a source of arbitrarily large photonic resource states, and doing it deterministically with microwave circuits removes the usual probabilistic overhead.
eli5.caveat: Thirteen photons is still small, and the error mitigation is built into the protocol, so the raw fidelity of the larger graphs and how it scales with size need a close look.

2610.21357.title: Stitched surface codes: planar concatenation through GHZ corridors
2610.21357.abstract: We present a fault-tolerant quantum-memory architecture that concatenates four distance-t rotated surface-code patches with the [[4,2,2]] outer code, encoding two logical qubits at code distance d = 2t in a physical footprint of N < 2(2t+1)^2 qubits on a square lattice with nearest-neighbor connectivity. The outer-code stabilizer generators XXXX and ZZZZ, each of physical weight 4t, are measured in situ via verified Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) ancillae distributed through narrow corridors between adjacent patches, without lattice surgery or long-range gates. The outer-code gadgets introduce hyperedge fault mechanisms, but by design each decomposes into graphlike components, so the complete syndrome is decoded by a single minimum-weight-perfect-matching pass. Circuit-level simulations show logical error rates that scale as p^t, consistent with distance-2t protection. Finally, we implement the construction experimentally on a 105-qubit Willow superconducting processor in both the ZZ and XX memory bases. With the correlated-matching decoder, increasing the code distance from d = 4 to d = 6 reduces the block logical error rate by a factor of 1.52. The construction thus provides a near-term testbed for concatenated architectures beyond the standard surface code.
2610.21357.why: Concatenating four surface-code patches with a [[4,2,2]] code via GHZ corridors runs on 105-qubit Willow, cutting logical error 1.52x from distance 4 to 6.

eli5.plain: They stitched four standard error-correcting patches together with a small outer code, and ran it on Google's Willow chip.
eli5.how: Big outer-code checks are measured by verified GHZ states threaded through narrow gaps between patches, so the decoder stays a single matching pass and the code distance doubles.
eli5.matters: A concrete, hardware-tested path to concatenated codes on plain nearest-neighbour lattices, without lattice surgery.
eli5.caveat: The experimental distance gain is a modest factor 1.52, smaller than ideal p^t scaling, and only memory is shown, not logical gates.

2610.20889.title: A Rydberg atom array coupled to a high-cooperativity optical cavity
2610.20889.abstract: Integrating Rydberg-state control of atom-atom interactions with cavity control of atom-light interactions enables the combination of local entangling operations with photon-mediated long-range coupling, measurement, and communication. Such integration is challenging because electric fields generated by charges on cavity optics and by cavity-stabilizing actuators may disturb Rydberg-state coherence. Here, we couple a Rydberg tweezer array to a high-cooperativity optical cavity, suppressing the electric fields produced by cavity length actuation so that the residual field variation of about $3~\mathrm{mV/cm}$ rms does not limit Rydberg coherence. We demonstrate two capabilities that neither system provides alone. First, we use Purcell-enhanced fluorescence to read out atoms directly in the ground-Rydberg basis within $7.5~μ\mathrm{s}$, well within the Rydberg-state lifetime, with ground- and Rydberg-state detection infidelities of $3\%$ and $5\%$, respectively, and with low atom loss. Second, we use Rydberg-Rydberg interactions to control collective light-atom scattering into the cavity mode. Specifically, we drive blockaded Rabi oscillations between a state with two ground-state atoms, which scatter collectively with a superradiant or subradiant rate controlled by the atomic positions, and an entangled state with a single Rydberg excitation, which scatters like a single atom. These capabilities open routes toward networked Rydberg processors, mid-circuit measurements in analog quantum simulators, and many-body quantum optics with entangled emitters coupled collectively to light.
2610.20889.why: Rydberg blockade switches two atoms between superradiant collective scattering and single-atom scattering into a high-cooperativity cavity, plus 7.5 us Purcell readout.

eli5.plain: They put an array of highly excited atoms inside a good optical cavity and showed that the atoms' interactions decide how brightly they shine into it together.
eli5.how: Two ground-state atoms scatter into the cavity collectively, brighter or dimmer depending on position; driving them into a blockaded state with one shared Rydberg excitation makes them scatter like one atom. The same cavity speeds up fluorescence for fast readout.
eli5.matters: Interactions switching collective emission on and off is waveguide- and cavity-QED physics the reader knows from transmons, here with a new knob that could inspire entangled-emitter experiments in circuits.
eli5.caveat: Two-atom demonstration; scaling to many entangled emitters and keeping Rydberg coherence near charged optics remain hard.

2610.16210.title: Collective Floquet engineering between two distant superconducting artificial atoms
2610.16210.abstract: A one-dimensional waveguide is a crucial medium for transferring propagating quantum information between remote qubits, yet the photon-mediated interaction is typically fixed by the static device geometry, qubit parameters, and their couplings to the transmission line. Such an interaction can be engineered to be coherent or dissipative via virtual- or real-photon exchange, respectively, yet its effective strength remains fixed in either case. Here we demonstrate dynamical control over this interaction by applying Floquet engineering to two superconducting qubits coupled to a waveguide terminated by a capacitive mirror. By positioning one qubit at an antinode and the other qubit at a node or an antinode of the resonant standing wave, we realize a Hermitian or non-Hermitian coupling between the two qubits. A periodic flux drive of the qubit frequencies then enables on-demand control of the coherent energy splitting and the collective decay. Our results establish Floquet engineering as a route to dynamically reshape both coherent and dissipative photon-mediated interactions between remote quantum emitters.
2610.16210.why: A flux drive turns the waveguide-mediated exchange and collective decay between two distant transmons into tunable, on-demand quantities instead of geometry-fixed ones.

eli5.plain: Two qubits far apart on the same microwave line normally talk to each other at a fixed strength; here they shake the qubit frequencies to dial that strength up and down at will.
eli5.how: A mirror at the end of the line makes a standing wave; putting the qubits at nodes or antinodes picks a coherent or a dissipative coupling, and a periodic flux modulation rescales both through Floquet sidebands.
eli5.matters: Dynamically switchable coherent and dissipative coupling between remote emitters is a direct tool for waveguide-QED gates, sub- and superradiance control, and state transfer.
eli5.caveat: Two qubits and one mirror geometry; whether the scheme survives with more emitters and without adding heating or sideband leakage is not shown.

2610.16493.title: Bell's go theorem: regaining local causality with a new notion of realism
2610.16493.abstract: Bell's theorem is popularly stated as the inconsistency of quantum theory with local realism. Realism is here formalized by the ontological models framework, where elements of reality are points of a measurable space and probabilities obey the Kolmogorov axioms. In the Bell scenario, locally causal ontological models posit a common cause supporting a global valuation, a joint assignment of outcomes to all measurements at once, across incompatible contexts. Within this notion of realism, Bell's theorem makes any realist explanation of the quantum predictions conspiratorial: any mechanism, whether superluminal, superdeterministic, or retrocausal, must be finely tuned so as never to manifest operationally. We redefine realism through a new ontological framework that generalizes the standard one. The elements of reality, which we call records, are no longer points but relational parts of a point-free generalization of a topological space (sublocales of a locale). A record shared by two incompatible contexts establishes the sameness of a measurement across them, without such pairwise identities composing into a global valuation, and the common cause is then a web of such records. Within this framework, Bell's no-go theorem becomes a go theorem: local causality, restated for records, is no longer at odds with the quantum statistics. This is possible because modularity, the inclusion-exclusion law of classical probability, fails across incompatible contexts, so that the probability theory generalizes Kolmogorov's. We exhibit explicit models reproducing several quantum strategies, including the optimal CHSH violation. More broadly, locally causal models of this kind attain every Bell-CHSH value up to the algebraic maximum. A realist explanation of the quantum predictions need not be conspiratorial; every causal influence posited by these models is reflected in the operational predictions.
2610.16493.why: Replacing points of an ontic space with point-free records on a locale yields locally causal, non-conspiratorial models reaching any CHSH value.

eli5.plain: They argue that Bell's theorem rules out local realism only for one particular idea of what 'real' means, and build a different idea under which local causes do explain quantum correlations.
eli5.how: Elements of reality become relational records shared between pairs of measurement contexts that never add up to a single global list of outcomes; probabilities then obey a weaker rule than Kolmogorov's, and local models reproduce the quantum statistics.
eli5.matters: It sharpens exactly which assumption Bell experiments, including superconducting-circuit ones, refute: the global joint valuation, not locality itself.
eli5.caveat: Whether giving up classical probability's additivity counts as 'realism' is a philosophical judgment, and the framework makes no new testable prediction.

2610.21853.title: Superconducting circuits host two-level systems with lifetimes exceeding one second
2610.21853.abstract: Understanding the microscopic environment of superconducting qubits is a central challenge for quantum technologies. Parasitic two-level systems (TLSs) of various microscopic origins are ubiquitous and limit qubit performance through decoherence, frequency drifts, and leakage. Recently, long-lived TLSs with lifetimes exceeding those of state-of-the-art qubits have been shown to induce correlated qubit dynamics, with direct implications for quantum error correction. Here, we perform wide-band quantum-jump correlation spectroscopy on flux-tunable transmon qubits and identify microscopic degrees of freedom that outlive the qubit by orders of magnitude. Pump-probe measurements at varying detunings from these objects reveal intrinsic lifetimes exceeding one second. Their weak coupling to the qubit, in the kilohertz range, is consistent with positional defects described by the standard tunneling model, without excluding other microscopic origins such as magnetic spin impurities or trapped quasiparticles. More broadly, these results establish superconducting qubits as a sensitive probe of exceptionally long-lived microscopic degrees of freedom and open a route toward their controlled access and functionalization.
2610.21853.why: Quantum-jump correlation spectroscopy finds TLS defects coupled at kilohertz to transmons whose intrinsic lifetimes exceed one second.

eli5.plain: They found tiny defects next to their qubits that hold an excitation for more than a second, millions of times longer than the qubit.
eli5.how: Watching correlations between qubit quantum jumps across a wide band of frequencies reveals hidden weakly coupled systems; pump-probe at varying detuning measures their own decay.
eli5.matters: Long-lived defects cause correlated qubit errors and drift, which matters directly for error correction and for interpreting T1 fluctuations.
eli5.caveat: The microscopic origin is open: tunnelling defects, spins or trapped quasiparticles all fit, and how common they are across fabs is unknown.

2610.19219.title: Selective Control and Imaging of Higgs and Goldstone Modes with a Quantum Simulator
2610.19219.abstract: We realize the mesoscopic Bose-Hubbard model at unit-filling on a two-dimensional array of transmon qubits and selectively excite collective modes associated with amplitude or phase fluctuations of the superfluid order parameter. We identify these modes respectively as the Higgs and Goldstone modes using complementary local observables, extracted from measuring the number of particles on each site. Modulation of the coupling between sites excites the Higgs mode, which we detect via the density of doubly occupied sites. In contrast, modulation of the local chemical potential with an appropriately chosen spatial profile excites the lowest-frequency Goldstone mode, which we detect via changes in the local density. The two modes have different symmetries and do not couple to one another. By varying the system geometry, we characterize the impact of finite system size on the evolution of both modes. In the thermodynamic limit, decay into a continuum of lower-energy excitations can obscure the Higgs response. In our mesoscopic system, however, the finite system size leads to spectral gaps and allows us to detect the Higgs mode as a coherent, long-lived excitation. Our work demonstrates how finite quantum simulators can isolate and probe physical phenomena that become difficult to resolve in the thermodynamic, large-scale limit.
2610.19219.why: Google's transmon Bose-Hubbard array selectively excites and images Higgs and Goldstone modes, with finite size keeping the Higgs mode coherent.

eli5.plain: On a grid of superconducting qubits behaving like interacting bosons, they kicked two different collective vibrations of the superfluid and watched each one separately.
eli5.how: Modulating hopping excites the amplitude (Higgs) mode, seen in doubly occupied sites; a shaped chemical-potential modulation excites the phase (Goldstone) mode, seen in local density.
eli5.matters: A clean demonstration of what mesoscopic analogue simulators can resolve that bulk systems blur, from a major hardware group.
eli5.caveat: The Higgs mode survives because the system is small; conclusions about the thermodynamic limit are indirect.

2610.23367.title: Bell scenarios encode classical non-causality
2610.23367.abstract: Bell and contextuality scenarios are unified within the Acín-Fritz-Leverrier-Sainz hypergraph formalism, in which measurements are hyperedges. Multipartite measurements are obtained from product rules that combine independent contextuality scenarios into a single hypergraph. Several such rules exist: they are structurally distinct, yet yield the same classical, quantum, and boxworld correlations. Here, we show that this difference is not incidental, unveiling an unexpected connection. The measurements of composite Bell scenarios are exactly the process functions, the deterministic classical communication protocols that may be non-causal, i.e., lack a definite causal order without generating paradoxes. Validity of a hyperedge and logical consistency of a process function are thus one and the same condition. This allows us to characterize process functions by normalization and no-signaling alone, providing transformations that generate non-causal process functions from no-communication ones. The product rules, in turn, order process functions by causal structure, from no-communication to non-causality, which yields a graphical criterion for the latter: a process function is non-causal precisely when its hyperedge is generated by the disjunctive but not the maximal product. We thereby obtain the first joint hypergraph representation of (non-causal) process functions and (nonlocal-without-entanglement) measurements, recasting classical non-causality as a non-standard way of composing black boxes.
2610.23367.why: The measurements of composite Bell scenarios are exactly the classical process functions, giving a graphical criterion for non-causal ones.

eli5.plain: They found that the rules for combining measurements in Bell experiments are the same mathematical objects as classical communication protocols without a fixed time order.
eli5.how: In the hypergraph formalism, a valid joint measurement and a logically consistent process function satisfy one and the same condition, so different product rules order processes from no-communication to non-causal.
eli5.matters: It ties indefinite causal order, now being tested with photons and circuits, to the familiar structure of Bell scenarios.
eli5.caveat: A structural classical result; it does not say whether non-causal processes exist in nature.

2610.17017.title: Photon-stimulated decay of $χ$-matched ancillas causes unheralded bit flips in bosonic codes
2610.17017.abstract: Bosonic codes often read out their syndrome with a transmon ancilla whose computational levels $g$ and $f$ have equal parity and matched dispersive shifts: a decay $f\to e$ is then heralded and leaves the code intact, while the direct $f\to g$ is forbidden by parity. We show that the photons of the code open this decay at first order in the ancilla's decay rate. Dressing by the code mode lets the charge noise that limits the ancilla's $T_1$ drive a photon-stimulated Raman decay $|f,n\rangle\to|g,n+1\rangle$, at $(n+1)(χ_{ge}/2g_{01})^2$ times the $f\to e$ rate for a smooth noise spectrum. When the matching is set by the detuning, the decay costs $\approxΓ_{fe}/α$ per gate and photon, whatever the coupling strength; a deliberate mismatch or matching by a drive lowers this cost, and a qubit ancilla has no such channel. The opened decay is unheralded and flips a cat with probability $\approx 1/2$; being first order, it overtakes the second-order double decay $f\to e\to g$ as the ancilla improves. In a microscopic model of the Ocelot repetition cat code, it makes the bit-flip floor of the gates grow linearly with the cat size, by a factor 1.2-1.7 from four to ten photons, which would limit the noise bias to $\sim 10^3$. The published gate data end at four photons and do not yet test this growth.
2610.17017.why: Code photons open a first-order unheralded f-to-g Raman decay of chi-matched ancillas, predicting bit-flip floors in Ocelot-style cat codes growing linearly with cat size.

eli5.plain: A theory paper showing that a trick used to protect bosonic codes from ancilla errors has a leak, opened by the code's own photons.
eli5.how: The code mode dresses the ancilla so charge noise can drive a decay from f to g while adding a photon; this flips the cat with probability one half and is not heralded.
eli5.matters: It predicts a concrete limit on the noise bias of AWS-style cat-qubit architectures and points to fixes such as deliberate mismatch or drive-based matching.
eli5.caveat: Model-based; the published gate data stop at four photons, so the predicted growth is still untested.

2610.16046.title: Measuring higher-order bulk topology in a programmable quantum simulator
2610.16046.abstract: Topological insulators lie outside the standard Landau paradigm: Instead of being characterized by local order parameters and spontaneous symmetry breaking, their defining properties are encoded in the global structure of their quantum states and manifested as robust boundary states. Crystalline higher-order topological insulators can extend this principle by hosting localized corner modes in two and higher dimensions. Although these boundary modes can be detected spectroscopically through the local density of states, determining the underlying bulk topology, for example through nested Wilson loops, remains an outstanding experimental challenge. Here we use up to 728 qubits in a superconducting analogue-digital quantum simulator to realize and probe a hierarchy of one-, two-, and three-dimensional topological insulators governed by effective tight-binding Hamiltonians. By reconstructing complex propagators from real-space measurements, we obtain complementary boundary and bulk characterizations: local densities of states reveal localized boundary modes, whereas experimentally reconstructed band projectors yield bulk topological invariants, culminating in a three-dimensional octupole moment extracted through third nested Wilson loops. These results establish a route to realizing, characterizing, and manipulating topologically protected states in programmable three-dimensional quantum matter.
2610.16046.why: Up to 728 qubits of an analogue-digital annealer realise 1D-3D higher-order topological insulators and extract a 3D octupole moment via nested Wilson loops.

eli5.plain: On a large superconducting quantum simulator they built models of exotic topological materials and measured their hidden bulk invariants, not just their edge states.
eli5.how: Real-space measurements reconstruct propagators, from which band projectors and nested Wilson loops give the bulk topological numbers.
eli5.matters: Shows a scale of programmable superconducting simulation, hundreds of qubits in 3D connectivity, that gate-based processors do not yet reach.
eli5.caveat: The physics is effectively single-particle tight-binding, so classical simulation is easy; the result is a capability demonstration rather than a quantum advantage.

2610.21428.title: Crossovers between Time-Bin and Energy-Time Entanglement in Homodyned Resonance Fluorescence
2610.21428.abstract: We theoretically investigate photonic entanglement generated by homodyning resonance fluorescence from a two-level emitter with a phase-locked laser field. Under weak excitation, increasing the relative laser-field amplitude produces crossovers from time-bin to energy--time and back to time-bin entanglement. The intermediate energy--time regime occurs near amplitude matching, where destructive interference suppresses the single-photon component, allowing the two-photon contributions to dominate the coincidence signal. We evaluate the resulting photon statistics and first-order coherence and characterize the entanglement through violations of the CHSH Bell inequality in a Franson interferometer. This scheme provides a route to controlling photonic entanglement through linear optics and coherent interference.
2610.21428.why: Homodyning resonance fluorescence with a phase-locked laser tunes the photon pair entanglement from time-bin to energy-time and back, verified via Franson CHSH.

eli5.plain: By mixing an emitter's glow with a bit of its own laser, they can choose which kind of entanglement the emitted photon pairs carry.
eli5.how: Near amplitude matching, interference cancels the single-photon part of the field so two-photon terms dominate; changing the relative amplitude moves the pair state between time-bin and energy-time entanglement.
eli5.matters: Homodyning a transmon's fluorescence with the drive is routine in waveguide QED, so this is a recipe that maps directly onto microwave experiments.
eli5.caveat: Theory in the weak-excitation limit; detector inefficiency and laser phase noise are not fully budgeted.

2610.22823.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
2610.22823.abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.
2610.22823.why: Under the standard composite-system representation and two textbook marginal claims, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to universality of POVMs.

eli5.plain: Usually people use the quantum measurement rules to prove you cannot signal; this paper runs it backwards and asks how much of those rules no-signaling forces.
eli5.how: Formalising the no-signaling hypothesis and the composite-experiment structure, they derive that every outcome probability must come from a POVM, and map which other postulates follow.
eli5.matters: Clarifies which parts of quantum measurement theory could be modified independently, a guide for anyone proposing deviations to test.
eli5.caveat: The result assumes the tensor-product representation of composite systems, which carries much of the weight.

2610.18778.title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
2610.18778.abstract: Multimode mechanical resonators offer a large set of densely packed, long-lived bosonic modes within a single compact device, making them attractive for quantum simulation, quantum information processing, and quantum-enhanced sensing. Many such applications rely on multipartite entanglement, yet deterministic mechanical entanglement has so far been largely limited to pairs of modes. Here we demonstrate the deterministic and programmable preparation of multipartite entangled states among the phonon modes of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator coupled to a superconducting transmon qubit. By sequentially applying optimal-control-engineered isometries between the qubit and successive modes, we generate matrix product states of bond dimension two, including $W$, Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ), and cluster states. We fully characterize these states via quantum state tomography and certify genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes. We further demonstrate correlated-noise sensing by exploiting the complementary decoherence responses of the stored $W$ and GHZ states, isolating inter-mode phase correlations from local decoherence and placing quantitative bounds on collective dephasing. Our results establish a scalable approach to preparing multipartite entangled states in mechanical systems, with promising applications in multiparameter sensing and tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects.
2610.18778.why: Optimal-control isometries from a transmon write W, GHZ and cluster states across up to four bulk-acoustic phonon modes, then use them to bound correlated dephasing.

eli5.plain: They used one superconducting qubit to tangle up to four sound modes in a crystal into the textbook multi-party entangled states.
eli5.how: The qubit is entangled with one phonon mode at a time through engineered pulses, building the state step by step like a chain; tomography then checks the whole state.
eli5.matters: It is the photonic sequential-generation recipe transplanted to phonons, showing that multimode acoustic resonators can be a dense, long-lived bosonic register for a circuit-QED lab.
eli5.caveat: Four modes with full tomography is a proof of principle; fidelities will drop quickly with more modes and the sensing demonstration is a bound, not a measured correlated-noise signal.

2610.18477.title: Experimental Realization of a C-Shunt Flux-Qubit Coupler for Controlled-Z Gates between Transmons
2610.18477.abstract: Fast entangling gates and low-interaction idling require distinct operating conditions in superconducting quantum processors. We experimentally realize a transmon-C-shunt-transmon (TCT) device in which a flux-tunable, three-junction capacitively shunted flux-qubit coupler connects two transmon data qubits. The C-shunt coupler provides a flux-tunable, positively anharmonic spectrum for tailoring the interactions between the data qubits. Conditional Ramsey and swap measurements identify an idle region with near-zero residual ZZ interaction strength and suppressed transverse exchange. At this bias, simultaneous single-qubit interleaved randomized benchmarking yields X-gate fldelities above 99.7%, consistent with individual operation. A 45 ns nonadiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gate achieves an interleaved randomized benchmarking fldelity estimate of 99.23(15)%. Numerical simulations identify coupler energy relaxation as an important limitation on CZ-gate fldelity and indicate that extending the coupler lifetime can improve gate performance. These results demonstrate the experimental feasibility of C-shunt flux-qubit couplers for combining low-interaction idling with fast entangling operations between transmon qubits.
2610.18477.why: A C-shunt flux-qubit coupler gives near-zero idle ZZ and a 45 ns CZ at 99.23% fidelity between transmons, limited by coupler T1.

eli5.plain: They used a different kind of qubit as the switch between two transmons, so the pair barely talks when idle but entangles fast when asked.
eli5.how: The flux-qubit coupler has positive anharmonicity that cancels the transmons' residual ZZ at one bias and enables a fast nonadiabatic CZ at another.
eli5.matters: Another coupler option to suppress idle crosstalk, with simulations pinpointing what to improve.
eli5.caveat: 99.23% CZ is below the current state of the art; the benefit hinges on making the coupler itself longer lived.

2610.14171.title: Experimental observation of Higgs oscillations and their power-law decay across pairing regimes in a cavity QED quantum simulator
2610.14171.abstract: Understanding how pairing correlations in superconductors evolve out of equilibrium is a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. In systems with $s$-wave pairing, the character of Cooper pairing evolves continuously from a BCS regime of weakly bound, overlapping pairs to a BEC regime of tightly bound molecules, each with distinct excitation spectra. Here we realize and probe pairing dynamics across these regimes using cold, non-degenerate $^{87}$Rb atoms coupled to an optical cavity with Floquet dressing. Our cavity-QED platform emulates fermionic superfluids through a mapping onto Anderson pseudospins, while optical and microwave control tunes the ratio of interactions to single-particle energies, providing a flexible approach complementary to ultracold Feshbach and ultrafast solid-state platforms. Following a quench, we observe persistent pairing and transient oscillations of the order parameter associated with a collective amplitude (Higgs) mode. We find that the decay of these oscillations sharply distinguishes weak- and strong-pairing regimes: in the weak-pairing regime, oscillations decay with a power-law exponent $|α|=0.65(8)$, whereas in the strong-pairing regime the decay is substantially faster, with $|α|>1$. The oscillation frequency is set by the minimum quasiparticle excitation energy, directly linking nonequilibrium dynamics to the underlying excitation spectrum. Our results establish nonequilibrium dynamics as a direct probe of pairing character and collective excitations in interacting quantum systems.
2610.14171.why: Floquet-dressed atoms in a cavity emulate BCS-to-BEC pairing and show Higgs oscillations decaying as a power law with exponent 0.65 in the weak-pairing regime.

eli5.plain: Using cold atoms that talk through an optical cavity, they mimic a superconductor and watch its order parameter ring after a sudden change.
eli5.how: Atoms are mapped onto pseudospins whose collective dynamics follows the same equations as Cooper pairs; the cavity mediates the interaction and quench dynamics are read out.
eli5.matters: Collective-mode physics of superconductors seen through a cavity-QED lens; the same mapping could be built with transmon arrays.
eli5.caveat: It is an emulation of mean-field pairing dynamics, not a real superconductor, and fluctuation effects beyond mean field are limited.

2610.18776.title: Quantum-enhanced mechanical sensing with machine-learning estimation
2610.18776.abstract: Massive mechanical oscillators couple directly to forces, accelerations and gravity, making them attractive probes of new physics and of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales. Pushing sensitivities beyond the standard quantum limit for signals of unknown phase requires non-Gaussian quantum states, whose metrological advantage has so far been confined to lighter systems such as trapped ions. Here we operate a microgram-scale acoustic mode of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator as a phase-insensitive quantum-enhanced sensor. A transmon qubit prepares the mode in Fock states of up to seven phonons by optimal control, and resolves its phonon-number distribution after interaction with a weak resonant signal. Bayesian analysis yields a Fisher information five times the vacuum value, a 7.0 dB gain in signal-amplitude sensitivity over any classical probe state, irrespective of its energy, currently limited by state preparation infidelities. We then train a neural network on the measured sensor response to perform Bayesian estimation without any analytical model of the system, showing the same sensitivity gain with half the systematic bias. Our results establish acoustic resonators prepared in non-Gaussian states as quantum-enhanced probes for high-frequency gravitational waves, dark matter and wave-function collapse.
2610.18776.why: Phonon Fock states up to seven quanta give a 7 dB phase-insensitive sensitivity gain in a microgram acoustic resonator, with a neural-network estimator matching it.

eli5.plain: They put a heavy sound resonator into states with an exact number of vibrations and showed it senses a weak push better than any classical state could.
eli5.how: A transmon prepares Fock states and later counts the phonons; a weak drive shifts the number distribution, and Bayesian or neural-network analysis turns that shift into an estimate of the drive.
eli5.matters: Fock-state sensing is a circuit-QED toolbox move; applying it to a massive oscillator links microwave quantum optics to dark-matter and collapse-model searches.
eli5.caveat: The gain is bounded by state-preparation infidelity and quoted against vacuum Fisher information; a real search would need long integration and calibrated backgrounds.

2610.21936.title: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
2610.21936.abstract: Far-detuned frequency allocations in fixed-frequency superconducting processors mitigate spectral crowding but constrain cross-resonance interactions at practical drive amplitudes. Here, we demonstrate that a single strong drive induces a large $XX-YY$ interaction in the far-detuned regime, while a weak second tone tunes the accompanying $ZZ$ phase. The interaction realizes a 150-ns $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gate, which can directly prepare a maximally entangled state from the ground state. For the implementations on the same qubit pair at matched drive strengths, cross resonance gives a shorter CNOT operation, while $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gives a 33% shorter SWAP operation with a higher IRB fidelity. The multilevel theory further predicts a regime where stronger driving can yield a speed advantage for CNOT as well, a possibility absent in the two-level model. As an application of the $XX-YY$ interaction, we also demonstrate two-spin squeezing beyond the standard quantum limit through two-axis countertwisting. The interaction realized here complements cross resonance and offers a route to efficient gate synthesis and quantum simulation of interacting spin systems.
2610.21936.why: Strong single-tone driving of far-detuned fixed-frequency transmons yields a 150 ns sqrt-bSWAP with tunable ZZ, beating cross-resonance for SWAP and showing two-spin squeezing.

eli5.plain: They found a way to make a strong exchange-like interaction between qubits that are far apart in frequency, giving faster SWAPs than the standard method.
eli5.how: A strong drive induces an XX minus YY interaction; a weak second tone sets the accompanying ZZ phase, and multilevel theory explains when strong driving speeds gates up.
eli5.matters: Useful for fixed-frequency architectures that spread qubit frequencies to avoid crowding.
eli5.caveat: Demonstrated on one pair; crosstalk and leakage at scale under strong drive remain open.

2610.20810.title: Syndrome-Resolved Decoding of Qubit Readout Errors
2610.20810.abstract: Readout errors in superconducting qubits include incorrect state assignment, bit flips within the computational subspace, and leakage to non-computational states. These errors require different mitigation strategies, yet conventional measurement fidelity and repeatability metrics do not resolve their individual contributions. Previous repeated-readout studies have shown that temporal correlations reveal additional information about readout errors. Here we introduce the Readout Error Decoder (RED), which converts repeated thresholded binary records into a channel-resolved error budget. Controlled error injections validate the channel-specific response of the decoder. We demonstrate RED on both fluxonium and transmon qubits and across distinct leakage-lifetime regimes. RED identifies the error channels limiting readout performance without requiring dedicated discrimination of non-computational states, providing a basis for targeted readout optimization across different qubit modalities.
2610.20810.why: A readout error decoder turns repeated thresholded records into a channel-resolved budget of misassignment, bit flips and leakage on fluxonium and transmon.

eli5.plain: They built a way to tell apart the different reasons a qubit reading comes out wrong, using only repeated ordinary readouts.
eli5.how: Temporal correlations in sequences of binary outcomes have different signatures for each error channel; a decoder fits these, validated by deliberate error injection.
eli5.matters: Targeted readout optimisation needs to know which channel dominates, and this needs no extra hardware.
eli5.caveat: Relies on a Markov model of the channels; non-Markovian effects or measurement-induced transitions may blur the separation.

2610.21754.title: Remote Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Entanglement Generation between Trapped Ions
2610.21754.abstract: Distributing entanglement directly between error-corrected logical qubits is an important capability for scalable quantum networks. We propose a heralded protocol for generating remote entanglement between Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill qubits encoded in the motional modes of spatially separated trapped ions, using the internal electronic states to interface the motional qubits with emitted photons. We derive the protocol for single-rail and polarization photonic encodings and evaluate the effects of finite GKP squeezing, photon loss, photon recoil, motional heating, and motional dephasing on the decoded logical state. Moreover, we numerically analysed the fidelity of distributed logical Bell-pair fidelity. We find that one can achieve more than 95% of fidelity in the realistic situation. The protocol combines motional-control and photonic-networking operations that have already been demonstrated in trapped-ion experiments.
2610.21754.why: A heralded photonic protocol entangles GKP qubits stored in the motion of distant trapped ions, with over 95% logical Bell-pair fidelity under realistic losses.

eli5.plain: A plan to link two error-protected quantum bits, stored in ion vibrations, across a distance using light.
eli5.how: The ion's internal state couples its GKP-encoded motion to an emitted photon; detecting photons from both ions heralds a logical Bell pair.
eli5.matters: Remote entanglement of bosonic logical qubits is exactly what microwave cat and GKP networks need; the protocol structure transfers.
eli5.caveat: Theory; the fidelity estimate rests on idealised photon collection and finite-squeezing models.

2610.21435.title: Accurate gap control of 3D-integrated superconducting quantum circuits using asymmetric indium architecture and multi-angle flip-chip bonding
2610.21435.abstract: Flip-chip 3D integration is a key enabling technology for overcoming the routing and layout constraints of planar superconducting quantum processors, but it requires accurate and uniform control of the inter-chip spacing while preserving qubit coherence. In conventional processes, thick indium bumps are deposited symmetrically on both chips, while dedicated spacers are introduced to limit the residual tilt. Here, we present a flip-chip bonding process based on an asymmetric indium architecture, combining $20\,μ\mathrm{m}$ thick indium bumps on the control chip with $200\,\mathrm{nm}$ thin indium pads on the qubit chip. Using electrical and microwave measurements, we demonstrate low resistance and low loss indium interconnects, and show that transmon qubits integrated with this process reach relaxation and coherence times of $T_1=(159\pm14)\,μ\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\mathrm{2,echo}}=(294\pm42)\,μ\mathrm{s}$, respectively, comparable to planar devices. Combined with a multi angle compression procedure that suppresses systematic tilt, this approach reduces the average post bonding tilt to $(20\pm12)\,μ\mathrm{rad}$. These results establish an asymmetric indium architecture combined with multi angle compression as a robust, coherence preserving route toward 3D-integrated superconducting quantum processors.
2610.21435.why: Thick indium bumps on one chip and thin pads on the other, plus multi-angle compression, give 20 microrad flip-chip tilt with T1 near 160 us.

eli5.plain: A better way to glue two chips face to face so the gap is uniform and the qubits stay good.
eli5.how: Asymmetric indium thicknesses and pressing from several angles cancel the systematic tilt without spacers.
eli5.matters: Flip-chip is how processors get past wiring limits; uniform gaps keep coupler and qubit parameters on target.
eli5.caveat: Coherence is comparable to planar devices, not better, and yield across large dies is not reported.

2610.17834.title: Broadening the reflection band of atomic mirrors by engineering the emitter-waveguide coupling
2610.17834.abstract: We theoretically investigate single-photon coherent transport through a finite waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) array with spatially modulated emitter-waveguide couplings. By combining exact scattering calculations with spectral factorization and a semiclassical WKB analysis, we identify how the coupling profile controls the reflection bandwidth and its finite-size dependence. A Gaussian transverse displacement produces an exponential-of-Gaussian decay-rate profile that broadens the high-reflectivity window and suppresses the boundary-induced Fabry-Perot oscillations compared with a uniform array. The transmission zeros remain exactly degenerate at the atomic resonance for arbitrary positive coupling profiles at non-Bragg spacings. In contrast, the collective poles reorganize under the spatial modulation, redistributing their radiative widths and preventing individual subradiant resonances from terminating the reflection window. We further derive an algebraic 1/N scaling law for the contraction of the bandwidth toward its bulk value. The bulk bandwidth is determined by the largest local decay rate, whereas the finite-size correction increases as the profile becomes sharper, leading to an optimal profile width. These results establish spatial coupling engineering as a practical tool for designing broadband atomic mirrors in atom-nanofiber and circuit-QED platforms.
2610.17834.why: A Gaussian profile of emitter-waveguide couplings widens the reflection band of a finite atomic mirror and kills its Fabry-Perot ripples, with a 1/N bandwidth law.

eli5.plain: They show that a row of artificial atoms reflects light over a wider band if the atoms are coupled more strongly in the middle and more weakly at the edges.
eli5.how: Exact scattering plus a WKB-style analysis: tapering the coupling softens the array's ends so collective resonances spread their widths instead of leaving narrow subradiant dips inside the band.
eli5.matters: Tapered transmon-waveguide coupling is easy to engineer in circuits, so this is a direct design rule for broadband qubit mirrors and photonic band edges.
eli5.caveat: Single-photon linear scattering only; disorder in qubit frequencies and nonlinear saturation, which dominate real transmon arrays, are not treated.

2610.17058.title: Architecting Instruction Execution for Scalable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
2610.17058.abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires orchestrating millions of operations continuously across a tightly coupled classical-quantum control stack. A critical challenge in this orchestration is determining the optimal hardware-software boundary, i.e., the Quantum Instruction Set Architecture (QISA). We focus on cryogenic, fixed-connectivity qubit platforms, such as superconducting and topological Majorana qubits. For these, existing QISA choices either operate at too low a level, violating cryogenic thermal budgets at scale, or at too high a level, imposing unrealizable complexity on the control engine. To reason about these tradeoffs, we introduce the ARIES instruction set hierarchy, which categorizes QISAs into distinct abstraction levels. To systematically evaluate these levels, we develop an end-to-end evaluation toolflow featuring a cycle-accurate classical driver and hardware engine simulator. Using eight quantum applications across superconducting and topological qubit platforms, we measure instruction bandwidth, transceiver power dissipation, and measurement processing overheads. We demonstrate that while physical-level abstractions exceed the thermal limits of dilution refrigerators by orders of magnitude, canonical-level abstractions significantly underestimate hardware routing congestion and execution runtimes. Our Level 4 QISA (local logical operations) offers an optimal architectural balance. As quantum hardware platforms scale toward FTQC in the coming years, our findings provide concrete architectural guidance for the design of their classical control stacks and instruction interfaces.
2610.17058.why: Microsoft's cycle-accurate study finds a local-logical-operation instruction set is the only level that fits cryogenic power budgets and realistic routing for FTQC.

eli5.plain: They asked at what level of detail a fault-tolerant quantum computer's instructions should be sent from the classical controller, and simulated the answer.
eli5.how: A hierarchy of instruction-set levels is evaluated with a cycle-accurate simulator on eight applications, measuring bandwidth, power and runtime.
eli5.matters: Control-stack design decides how many wires and how much heat go into the fridge, a real bottleneck for scaling.
eli5.caveat: Simulation with assumed hardware parameters; the conclusions shift with control electronics that do not exist yet.

2610.17300.title: Ghost unitaries for loss-resilient photonic resource-state generation
2610.17300.abstract: Entangled few-photon states, such as Bell and Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states, are central resources for discrete-variable photonic quantum information processing. In many architectures, these states are generated probabilistically by first heralding single photons from biphoton sources and then interfering them in linear-optical circuits. In this work, we show that the entanglement structure of said biphoton sources can be directly exploited for noise-engineering to deliver higher quality resource states. Using the transpose identity of multi-mode squeezed vacuum states, we introduce "ghost-unitary" implementations in which the target resource-generation interferometer is applied to the heralding modes rather than to the delivered resource modes. When the dominant imperfection is interferometric loss, this relocation converts direct amplitude damping of the output into false-positive heralding events that require both higher-pair emission and photon loss. In the low-squeezing regime, these events are parametrically suppressed, yielding higher-fidelity conditional resource states. We analyze this mechanism for single-qubit states, two-photon NOON states, Bell states, and a family of $n$-qubit GHZ states, as well as for single-qubit teleportation and type-I-fusion-based resource growth. Across these examples, we delineate finite parameter regimes in which ghost-unitary implementations outperform direct implementations, with particular relevance to frequency-bin photonics where active linear-optical transformations can be relatively lossy. We also prove that, in the setting considered here, the direct implementation of the $n$-GHZ family delivers identically damped outputs: equivalent to the ideal state followed by uniform amplitude damping. This extends the known $n=2,3$ cases and provides a structural result of independent interest for photonic quantum information processing.
2610.17300.why: Applying the interferometer to the heralding arms of squeezed sources converts loss into rare false heralds, raising resource-state fidelity; direct GHZ outputs are uniformly damped.

eli5.plain: A trick for making entangled photon states: do the lossy optical processing on the partner photons you detect, not on the photons you keep.
eli5.how: For multi-mode squeezed vacuum, an operation on one side equals its transpose on the other; moving the lossy circuit to the herald side turns loss into false alarms that need both loss and double pairs.
eli5.matters: A neat loss-relocation idea that could carry over to microwave two-mode-squeezing sources with lossy routing.
eli5.caveat: Benefits appear only in the low-squeezing regime, which means low rates.

2610.20752.title: Schrödinger's unpublished hidden-variable model in the 1944-45 debate over the "Collapse of Determinism"
2610.20752.abstract: In the mid-1940s, the question of whether quantum mechanics could be supplemented by deterministic hidden variables resurfaced in a debate in ^textit{Nature}. I show that Erwin Schrödinger drafted a hitherto unpublished response to this controversy. In it, Schrödinger provided an explicit hidden-variable model, thereby showing that such models could not be ruled out. I reconstruct the historical context of this forgotten manuscript and publish here the first transcription and analysis. Importantly, Schrödinger's proposal should be understood as a proof of principle rather than as evidence of his commitment to determinism.
2610.20752.why: An unpublished 1944-45 Schrödinger manuscript gives an explicit hidden-variable model, transcribed and analysed for the first time.

eli5.plain: A historian found a never-published note in which Schrödinger wrote down a working hidden-variable model in the 1940s.
eli5.how: Archival reconstruction of the Nature debate on the 'collapse of determinism' and a transcription of the manuscript with analysis.
eli5.matters: It corrects the history of the hidden-variable debate before Bohm and Bell.
eli5.caveat: Historical; the model itself is a proof of principle and adds nothing beyond later results.

2610.20132.title: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
2610.20132.abstract: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. We present a low-cost, compact muon detector consisting of two plastic scintillator modules, each read out by a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), operated in coincidence. We characterize the SiPMs from room temperature down to 10 mK, including the breakdown and upper-limit voltages that define the operating bias range. Operated as a muon counter, the detector measures a coincidence rate that, as expected, is independent of temperature within uncertainties and agrees with analytical and Monte Carlo predictions. Below approximately 8 K, each muon event produces two pulses, one narrow and one broad, an effect that, to our knowledge, has not been reported before. Coincidences with an independent muon detector outside the cryostat confirm that muons are still counted reliably in this regime. By studying the appearance of double pulses as a function of temperature and magnetic field up to 4.5 T, we find a behavior consistent with the phase diagram of a type-II superconductor. This links the double pulses to a superconducting material in the SiPM, likely an adhesion layer or diffusion barrier introduced during manufacturing. The mechanism by which the superconducting state produces the second pulse is not yet understood.
2610.20132.why: A cheap in-cryostat scintillator muon tagger works to 10 mK and reveals unexplained double pulses tied to a superconducting layer in the SiPM.

2610.19304.title: Leakage benchmarking with decohering subgroups in the presence of preparation and measurement errors
2610.19304.abstract: A common problem with physical qubits is that the state can leak outside the computational subspace. To characterize the problem, it is desirable to measure both the leakage probability and the fidelity of gates inside the computational subspace. Randomized benchmarking is a readily accessible method for estimating average gate fidelities and can be modified to account for leakage. However, in the presence of state preparation and measurement errors (SPAM) there are parameter degeneracies, and fidelities and leakage become underdetermined. We study the example of qudits with any number of leakage levels under the assumption of gate-independent noise. We show that randomized benchmarking sequences with leakage level decoherence can be analyzed as a Markov process with noisy classical preparations and measurements. This result generalizes to randomized benchmarking with random gates from an arbitrary group that contains a phase-decohering subgroup. We characterize the parameter degeneracy in inferring the Markov process, preparations and measurements. Based on this characterization we develop a measurement and inference method taking advantage of known conservative bounds on SPAM to constrain fidelity, leakage and other parameters of the Markov process, state preparations and measurements. As part of our study, we experimentally implemented the measurement method for a qubit defined on the one-excitation subspace of two transmons, for which there are two leakage levels. We determined confidence intervals accounting for parameter degeneracy for a number of performance parameters of the system. For leakage and fidelity, we compare these intervals to those obtained for several conventional methods for leakage benchmarking.
2610.19304.why: Randomized benchmarking with leakage is recast as a Markov process with noisy classical SPAM, yielding SPAM-robust confidence intervals for leakage and fidelity.

2610.19180.title: Cavity-assisted dynamic nuclear polarisation
2610.19180.abstract: Dynamic nuclear polarisation transfers polarisation from electron to nuclear spins by relying on a dissipative channel. Here we introduce a cavity-based DNP mechanism which uses the radiative relaxation of the electronic spin through the Purcell effect to bring about the nuclear spin polarisation. We implement this protocol on an ensemble of bismuth donor spins (I=9/2, S=1/2) in isotopically purified silicon coupled to a superconducting resonator. A single cycle, combining adiabatic microwave and radio-frequency pulses with Purcell relaxation, increases a target ground state's population by a factor of $1.79\pm0.04$; a cumulative enhancement of $4.6\pm0.2$ is reached with additional cycles, to be compared with the theoretical limit of ninefold set by the degeneracy of the ground manifold. We explain this difference by the competition between Purcell and intrinsic relaxation on the one hand and a collective effect that slows down the electronic spin radiative decay as the nuclear spin population grows on the other hand. Our results place radiative DNP as an available mechanism at millikelvin temperatures where phonon-mediated relaxation is frozen.
2610.19180.why: Purcell-enhanced spin relaxation into a superconducting resonator drives nuclear polarisation of bismuth donors, reaching 4.6-fold enhancement at millikelvin temperatures.

eli5.plain: They use a microwave cavity to cool electron spins quickly and, by doing it the right way, drag the nuclear spins into one chosen state.
eli5.how: Adiabatic microwave and radio-frequency pulses swap populations, then the electron spin emits its energy into the resonator via the Purcell effect, a loop that ratchets nuclear population into the target level.
eli5.matters: It turns radiative cavity relaxation into a resource for spin-ensemble initialisation, relevant to spin-based microwave memories coupled to circuits.
eli5.caveat: The enhancement stalls at about half the theoretical ninefold, limited by a collective slowdown of radiative decay the authors only partly model.

2610.22097.title: Operational Limits of Gravity-Mediated Entanglement
2610.22097.abstract: Tests of gravity-mediated entanglement aim to determine whether two massive objects in spatial superposition can become entangled through their mutual gravitational interaction. In an ideal model, the two objects are often treated as pointlike branches, but real wave packets have a finite width and are also exposed to dephasing and residual non-gravitational forces. We study these effects in a two-branch gravitational cat-state model with Gaussian wave packets. The Newtonian interaction is averaged over the finite wave-packet width, and spatially correlated dephasing is included phenomenologically. We then ask a practical question: when does the generated state remain useful rather than merely entangled? To answer this, we examine Bell violation, teleportation fidelity, coherent information, Fisher information, and state distinguishability. We find finite parameter windows where the same state is Bell-nonlocal and teleportation-useful, but these windows shrink as the wave packets become broader or the dephasing becomes stronger. We also show that a residual electrostatic branch interaction can coherently cancel the gravitational nonlocal phase and strongly suppress the operational signal. The results identify finite-width and electrostatic tolerance boundaries that should be considered in future tests of gravity-mediated entanglement.
2610.22097.why: Finite wave-packet width and dephasing shrink the windows where gravity-mediated entangled states are Bell-nonlocal; residual electrostatics can cancel the gravitational phase.

eli5.plain: They checked how realistic imperfections spoil the planned tabletop tests of whether gravity can entangle two masses.
eli5.how: Averaging the gravitational phase over Gaussian wave packets and adding correlated dephasing, they track Bell violation and other usefulness measures.
eli5.matters: Sets tolerance targets for gravity-entanglement experiments, the flagship foundations test of the decade.
eli5.caveat: Dephasing is phenomenological and the model is two-branch; real experiments face many more noise sources.

2610.23810.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
2610.23810.abstract: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at $f_s$ is indistinguishable from one at $f_p - f_s$, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180$^{\circ}$ hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.
2610.23810.why: Two kinetic-inductance TWPAs between 180-degree hybrids give 20 dB gain over nearly an octave with -15 dB image rejection, doubling usable bandwidth.

2610.18124.title: Local error correction prolongs time-crystalline memory
2610.18124.abstract: Discrete time crystals are non-equilibrium phases of matter with spatiotemporal order and a response that breaks the time-translation symmetry of a periodic external drive. Interactions, spatial disorder and correlated random driving can in theory stabilize this order. In experiments, however, coupling to the environment limits the time crystal lifetime. Here we use stochastic local bit-flip error correction to prolong the time-crystalline response of a driven, spatially disordered two-dimensional Ising model on a superconducting quantum processor, using a repetition code with distances three and five on a honeycomb lattice with up to 68 physical qubits. Even though ancilla qubits, midcircuit syndrome measurements and decoding increase the required quantum and classical resources, the stochastic drive increases the memory decay time by a factor of up to two. At late times we observe that recovery stabilizes spatial order across the lattice. The spin-configuration distributions explain this separation, as recovery suppresses disagreeing bonds while broadening occupies completely reversed states. Syndrome measurements without correction accelerate the memory decay, demonstrating the importance of conditional correction. Our results show that local bit-flip error correction can preserve time-crystalline memory over more drive cycles than the bare dynamics.
2610.18124.why: Repetition-code bit-flip correction on up to 68 qubits doubles discrete time-crystal memory lifetime; syndrome measurement without correction shortens it.

2610.21684.title: Quantum instanton approach to metastable collective spin systems: Numerical implementation and applications
2610.21684.abstract: Driven-dissipative collective spin systems can host several long-lived metastable states; rare switching between them governs slow relaxation and first-order dissipative phase transitions associated with changes in the dominant stationary state. In the companion Letter [arXiv:2604.15091], we introduced a quantum instanton framework based on exact quasiprobability dynamics to describe this switching and illustrated it with a minimal model possessing a simplifying symmetry. Here we develop its numerical implementation, combining collocation and shooting methods, and apply it to two microscopically motivated systems: the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model with purely collective dissipation and the cooperative resonance fluorescence with collective and local dissipation. By determining the leading exponential scaling of switching rates between metastable attractors, we predict the stationary magnetization, the first-order dissipative phase-transition point, and the exponential scaling of slow relaxation rates. These predictions agree with quantum master-equation calculations and an exact analytical result for the second model without dephasing. We also examine how the choice of quasiprobability representation affects numerical convergence and find that the alternative semiclassical Wigner approach, based on Gaussian truncation, has varying accuracy across models and parameter regimes. These results substantiate the framework's applicability to experimentally relevant collective spin systems with both collective and local dissipation.
2610.21684.why: Quantum instanton numerics predict switching rates, stationary magnetisation and first-order transitions in cooperative resonance fluorescence, matching master-equation results.

eli5.plain: A numerical method to predict how often a driven, lossy collection of spins jumps between two long-lived states.
eli5.how: Exact quasiprobability dynamics give an action whose minimal path, the instanton, sets the exponential switching rate.
eli5.matters: Driven-dissipative bistability is common in nonlinear microwave resonators and transmon arrays; this gives a quantitative handle on it.
eli5.caveat: Collective-spin models only; extension to genuinely many-body local interactions is not shown.

2610.16198.title: Time-Frequency Continuous-Variable Quantum Teleportation with Single Photons
2610.16198.abstract: Quantum teleportation, a key building block for quantum technologies, enables distant parties, Alice and Bob, to transfer an unknown quantum state using entanglement, local operations, and classical communication. In this work, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for single-photon time-frequency continuous variables, where time is the time of arrival at a detector. We detail the operational requirements of the protocol, notably the nonlinear interactions needed for the photon-photon time-frequency entangling gate. By explicitly treating the detector position as the reference frame for time of arrival, we show that, even with ideal classical and quantum channels, the input-output fidelity is not unity unless the receiving party can correct the detector-position mismatch. This results in a trade-off between teleportation fidelity and the temporal bandwidth of the input photon wavepacket. The protocol itself can be used for remote detector synchronization. In particular, we show that time-frequency cat and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states provide an internal temporal ruler through fidelity revivals. We further derive the classical and best-copy fidelity thresholds for single-photon Gaussian wavepackets, finding that the relevant vacuum-equivalent shot noise is input-dependent, in contrast with quadrature-based continuous-variable quantum teleportation. Our proposal derives from a quantum theory of space-time events, whereafter we establish space as a reference for the time degree of freedom, thereby grounding our work in ongoing research on reference frames and superselection rules in quantum optics and quantum information. Beyond protocols harnessing time-frequency continuous variables of single photons, this work points toward remote synchronization in quantum communication architectures.
2610.16198.why: Continuous-variable teleportation in single-photon time-frequency needs detector-position correction; time-frequency cat and GKP states give fidelity revivals for synchronisation.

eli5.plain: A proposal to teleport the timing and colour of a single photon, which shows the receiver must know where its detector sits.
eli5.how: Treating arrival time as a continuous variable, the detector position acts as a reference frame; a mismatch limits fidelity unless corrected, trading against the photon's bandwidth.
eli5.matters: Time-frequency encodings are natural for shaped microwave photons, and the reference-frame point applies to any remote node synchronisation.
eli5.caveat: Requires photon-photon nonlinear gates that are not available at useful efficiency.

2610.17225.title: Quantum Reference Frames in terms of Tetrads
2610.17225.abstract: We adapt to the context of quantum theory the treatment, familiar in relativity theory, of a reference frame as a tetrad. Since a tetrad is a set of four orthonormal vectors at a spacetime point, it encodes a timelike direction, three orthogonal spatial directions, and units; and so it gives a configuration in spacetime (a spatial orientation and state of motion) of an idealized infinitesimal apparatus (``rulers and a clock"). So a natural ``first guess" is that the state of a quantum reference frame should be an assignment of complex amplitudes to a set of tetrads. We develop this idea, in terms of bundles over spacetime of bases of the tangent spaces. This paper is a companion to two other papers. It emphasises the main conceptual aspects of our proposal, while the other two papers give physical details. It also explains the main contrast between those two papers. Namely: (i) the first considers a single spacetime geometry, so that a quantum reference frame, on our proposal, gives a superposition of perspectives on that geometry; while (ii) the second considers the spacetime manifold with no geometry given a priori, which will imply that a quantum reference frame, on our proposal, can describe a superposition of perspectives on a superposition of geometries---not ``just" a superposition of perspectives on a single geometry. The main mathematical idea for representing this contrast will be choosing between (i) the orthonormal frame bundle, for a given spacetime geometry; (ii) the frame bundle in the usual sense of containing all bases of all spacetime points' tangent spaces.
2610.17225.why: Quantum reference frames are modelled as amplitudes over tetrads on frame bundles, allowing superpositions of perspectives on superposed geometries.

eli5.plain: A proposal for what a quantum version of a lab's rulers and clocks should be, borrowed from how relativity describes reference frames.
eli5.how: A quantum frame is a wavefunction over tetrads; using the orthonormal or the full frame bundle distinguishes a fixed spacetime from a superposition of spacetimes.
eli5.matters: Conceptual groundwork for quantum-gravity-flavoured foundations and for questions of what an observer's perspective means.
eli5.caveat: This is the conceptual companion paper; the physical details and any predictions are in the other two.

2610.22145.title: Gyrators for superconducting circuit design
2610.22145.abstract: Assuming only the solubility of Kirchhoff's laws, the conservation of energy, and the form of the constitutive relations, we present a flux-charge symmetric Hamiltonian formalism that always admits a symplectic reduction for nonsingular, well-posed circuits involving gyrators, inductors, and capacitors (LCG circuits) with arbitrary non-linearity. The formalism introduces a notion of circuit duality on non-linear non-reciprocal circuits and a family of point transformations that inserts, removes, and moves reciprocal elements across gyrators while preserving the Hamiltonian spectrum. With these transformations, we extend Tellegen's classic result that gyrators make reciprocal elements behave as their dual to non-linear reciprocal elements such as the Josephson junction and quantum phase slip. Furthermore, we present conditions under which non-reciprocal circuits can be transformed to dynamically equivalent reciprocal circuits.
2610.22145.why: A flux-charge symmetric Hamiltonian formalism handles nonlinear gyrator circuits and moves Josephson elements across gyrators while preserving the spectrum.

2610.20670.title: Mechanical trisqueezing in circuit quantum acoustodynamics with SNAIL devices
2610.20670.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum information processing with mechanical oscillators requires a uni- versal gate set, including a genuine non-Gaussian evolution. While circuit quantum acoustodynamics (cQAD) experiments have realized bilinear and quartic (four-wave mixing) operations by coupling mechanical modes to transmon qubits, the intrinsic Kerr nonlinearity of these devices precludes access to odd-order effective Hamiltonians such as trisqueezing. Here we propose a cQAD architec- ture in which a mechanical mode, hosted in a high-overtone bulk acoustic-wave resonator (HBAR), is coupled to a superconducting nonlinear asymmetric inductive element (SNAIL). By combining the cubic nonlinearity of the SNAIL with parametric flux driving, we engineer a three-wave mixing interaction that generates trisqueezed mechanical states, producing the characteristic triangular, star-shaped Wigner function with negative regions indicative of non-Gaussianity. We derive the effective trisqueezing Hamiltonian from the full circuit model, identify the drive frequencies and flux modulation required to isolate the desired interaction from competing terms, and quantify the achievable coupling strengths for parameters compatible with current fabrication capabilities. Our results establish a hardware-efficient route to non-Gaussian resource generation in mechanical quantum systems, extending the toolbox of cQAD toward universal continuous-variable quantum computation and enhanced quantum-limited sensing.
2610.20670.why: A SNAIL's cubic nonlinearity with flux pumping yields a three-phonon trisqueezing Hamiltonian for a bulk acoustic resonator, with realistic coupling estimates.

eli5.plain: A proposal to make a vibrating crystal hold a three-fold star-shaped quantum state that cannot be made by ordinary squeezing.
eli5.how: Couple the acoustic mode to a SNAIL, an element with a cubic rather than quartic nonlinearity, and pump its flux at the right frequency so three phonons are created or destroyed together.
eli5.matters: Odd-order non-Gaussian operations are scarce in circuit QED; a native trisqueezer would widen the bosonic-mode toolbox beyond Kerr-based tricks.
eli5.caveat: Theory only; competing terms are suppressed on paper but the achievable rate versus phonon and SNAIL loss decides whether the star-shaped Wigner function survives.

2610.18980.title: Transmission representation of the Josephson free energy beyond the short-junction limit
2610.18980.abstract: Beenakker's formula, $U(\varphi)-U(0)=Δ\sum_n\bigl(1-\sqrt{1-τ_n\sin^2(\varphi/2)}\bigr)$, expresses the zero-temperature energy-phase relation of a short Josephson junction through its normal-state transmission eigenvalues. We generalize this transmission representation beyond the short-junction limit and express the phase-dependent free energy of a time-reversal-symmetric $s$-wave junction as a Matsubara sum over channels with frequency-dependent transmissions. The representation constrains the small-phase expansion of the free energy. In particular, we prove that the normalized ratio of its quartic and quadratic coefficients satisfies $-1\leα_r\le7/80$ at finite temperature. We also construct a four-site junction with $α_r>0$, which disproves the conjectured upper bound $α_r\le0$. So that these results can be trusted without repeating the derivations, every numbered equation is formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.
2610.18980.why: Beenakker's transmission formula is generalised beyond short junctions, bounding the quartic-to-quadratic ratio and disproving a conjecture, all verified in Lean.

2610.17163.title: Bosonic unstructured search: quantum enhancement without entanglement
2610.17163.abstract: We consider unstructured search using multimode bosonic quantum systems under energy constraints. The task is to locate an unknown marked mode among $N$ possibilities using arbitrary control, subject to a time-averaged mean-boson-number budget $n_{\text{b}}\gg 1$. We analyze a continuous-time phase-shift oracle of strength $B_{0}$, with cost given by the total oracle time, and a discrete oracle with fixed phase $φ_{0}$, with cost given by the number of queries. We give algorithms that identify the target with query complexity $O(\sqrt{N}/{n_{\text{b}}}B_{0})$ for continuous-time oracles or $O(\sqrt{N}/n_{\text{b}} |{\sin(φ_{0}/{2})}|)$ for discrete oracles with $n_{\text{b}} |{\sin(φ_{0}/{2})}|=O(1)$.
